- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.40) — model fails to capture sharp downside momentum.
- Lag in price corrections: model often delays mean reversion after spikes, especially when sentiment turns negative.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves: model overreacts to recent highs, leading to overestimation in the following 5–7 days.
- Underweight sentiment in long-term (30d) forecasts — sentiment decay is not sufficiently reflected in model’s horizon adjustment.
- Model exhibits “sticky” bias toward recent highs — fails to reset forecast baseline when sentiment shifts sharply downward.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.30–0.40), model overfits short-term noise and underperforms in medium-term (15–30d) horizon.
